machine.gpu: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition

context.note: 10,000 Japanese characters. Japanese runs 0.516 tokens per character, so the token count is the number that matters and both are given.

method: Median of seven, first three discarded. Device time only: the engine is called in process, so no transport is included. The baseline is vLLM on the same card with VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0, which it needs on this architecture.

whole_job.note: One context, N questions. Prismyra is flat to 32 because a traversal costs the same whatever it carries; the staircase steps every 32.
whole_job.vllm_model: 87 ms for the context plus 47 ms per question. The per-question figure is measured; multiplying it is an extrapolation, and it is vLLM used straightforwardly -- padding contexts to block multiples and submitting every question in one batch are untested workarounds that would narrow the gap.

cost_model.note: At about 5,000 context tokens. Both constants grow with the context.

context_pass_steps.note: Each step is its own paired run: the same process measures with and without that one change. The chain is therefore not continuous -- one step's 'after' and the next step's 'before' differ by a few milliseconds of run-to-run variation, and both are reported rather than smoothed.

steps.change: routed experts on a fused kernel
dense projections on a block-scaled fp8 kernel
convolution on a Triton kernel written for it

kernels_against_vllm.note: Same work, same card, from profiles of both. Lower is better.

branch_pass.note: One group of up to 32 questions, at the same context length.

several_users.note: Four users with different contexts and two questions each. Their context passes share one traversal; their branch passes do not yet.
several_users.choices_unchanged: 8 of 8 against each user run alone

queue.note: Eight requests arriving together, from a run predating the kernel work; the shape is what matters, not the absolute values.
